blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang on Tuesday hit back at Vice President Sara Duterte’s camp over its allegation that the Marcos administration was behind an alleged threat against a former member of her household staff, accusing the previous Duterte administration of being adept at planting evidence. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was focused on economic recovery and strengthening the country’s relations with fellow members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) and its dialogue partners, rather than engaging in political intrigue. “Creating intrigue and planting evidence are not things we do at this time.
